blocks.text: Why PR managers choose Notion on Mac

Public relations managers often deal with high volumes of information. You juggle media lists, pitch schedules, and press release drafts. Notion helps you organize these tasks in one place. On a Mac, the desktop app feels fast and responsive. You can use ⌘ P to find any document in seconds. This saves time when you need to pull a contact name or a campaign date during a busy day.

A media list is the backbone of your PR work. Instead of a static spreadsheet, use a Notion database. Create properties for journalist names, outlets, and beats. You can filter this list by outlet or topic. Use a Select property for the status of your outreach. This makes it easy to see who you have already contacted.

items: Create a new page and type /database to start.
Add a Select property for 'Outlet Type' like Print or Online.
Use a Date property for 'Last Contacted' to track your history.
Filter your view to show only 'Pending' pitches.

blocks.text: Campaign management requires visibility. Use a Board view to see every stage of your campaign. Create columns for 'Drafting', 'Review', 'Sent', and 'Follow-up'. Drag and drop your tasks as they move through the pipeline. This visual approach helps you spot bottlenecks before they become urgent problems.
Use the /board command in a database to switch views instantly. This lets you toggle between a calendar and a board without losing your data.
blocks.title: Switch views quickly

blocks.text: Consistency is key for press releases. Create a database template that includes your standard header, boilerplate, and media contact info. When you start a new draft, click the arrow next to the 'New' button to select your template. This ensures you never miss a required section for your clients.
Speeding up your workflow on Mac

Notion supports standard Mac keyboard shortcuts. Use ⌘ B for bold and ⌘ I for italics. To see all available shortcuts, press ⇧ ? in the app. Using these shortcuts helps you keep your hands on the keyboard. This reduces the time spent switching between your mouse and your text.

items: Keeping all your data in one massive page instead of using databases.
Forgetting to set permissions when sharing pages with external clients.
Ignoring the filter feature when your database grows too large.
Not using templates for recurring tasks like weekly reports.

blocks.text: Start by auditing your current PR workflow. Identify one process that feels slow, such as updating your media list. Move that data into a Notion database. Once you are comfortable, add a board view for your campaign tracking. If you need help with a specific step, ask Lazur to guide you through the interface.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for media lists on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, Notion is ideal for media lists. You can use databases to store contact info, track outreach history, and filter by journalist beats.

faq.question: How do I speed up my work in Notion?
faq.answer: Use keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ P to search and ⇧ ? to view the full list of commands. Also, use templates for recurring tasks like press releases.

faq.question: Is Notion better than a spreadsheet for PR?
faq.answer: Notion offers more flexibility. You can link databases, add comments to rows, and switch between board, calendar, and list views.

faq.question: What if I get stuck in Notion?
faq.answer: You can check the official Notion help center or use a tool like Lazur to ask how to perform specific tasks while you are in the app.
